transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-25 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Kaitlyn (Redwood CSM), Priya (Lumina CISO), Jenna (Lumina InfoSec), Tom (Lumina Platform), Ravi (Lumina SRE)

Auto-summary: quick run through pen test, triage of critical/high flaws, agree remediation owners and verify patch strategy and timelines.

[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for making time, we'll keep to 55 minutes, we want to run through the penetration test findings, remediation plan, and then patch cadence — sound good?
[00:24] Priya (Lumina): Yep that's good, we want to make sure the high sev stuff is triaged and we understand any exposure windows.
[00:37] Marco (Redwood-SE): Quick intro from me — Marco, I work on infra and security for Redwood inference runtime, I'll focus on exploitable vectors, patch playbook and verification approach.
[00:50] Jenna (Lumina): Thanks, Jenna here — I own pen-test coordination and will log the tickets.
[01:12] Tom (Lumina): Tom, platform eng, I'll be doing the patching and rolling restarts on clusters.
[01:25] Ravi (Lumina): Ravi, SRE, focusing on rollback plans and deployment windows.
[01:40] Aisha: Cool. Quick housekeeping — we'll share the SOC2 and ISO artifacts and the pen-test summary after the call. Marco will walk through the top findings.
[02:05] Marco: ok jumping in, slide deck is in the chat (link: https://redwood.internal/decks/pen-test-summary) — first observation: a handful of critical findings relate to outdated third-party libs on our inference runtime container. Some are dependency chaining, some are CVE-elevations.
[02:40] Jenna: That aligns with the vendor report — they flagged 3 critical CVEs and 6 high.
[03:05] Marco: Right, the critical ones are in the image build step — glibc/openssl variants — patch available but needs rebuild/test. We recommend a rebuild + smoke test then canary roll.
[03:30] Priya: How long is the typical rebuild and canary? We need an estimate for exposure window.
[03:44] Marco: For a single service rebuild and canary — about 2-4 hours end-to-end including validation depending on test coverage; full fleet depends on size, expect 1-2 days with phased rollouts and busy windows.
[04:05] Tom: Our concern is rolling across prod during peak trading hours — can we do rolling during low volume?
[04:18] Ravi: We also need a backout plan if the quantization path hits perf regressions.
[04:30] Marco: Agreed — we suggest staging validation with perf microbenchmarks and a fallback to previous image; Redwood supports KV cache warming so we can run perf tests in staging first.
[04:58] Jenna: Aisha — can you confirm if Redwood provides patch playbooks or runbooks we can follow?
[05:10] Aisha: Yes, Marco has a remediation playbook template — he'll share it after the call.
[05:23] Marco: I'll share a playbook with steps: rebuild image, run unit/integration/ perf smoke, canary 5% traffic, monitor latency/errs for 3 hours, then 25% 50% 100%. Also include rollback commands.
[05:45] Priya: Ok. Next — there were a couple of auth/RBAC issues the testers flagged where service-to-service tokens were overly permissive.
[05:58] Marco: I saw that — it's primarily IAM policy scope on the internal controller; recommended: tighten roles, enforce least privilege and rotate service keys.
[06:15] Tom: We use our internal vault + AWS KMS to wrap keys — is Redwood compatible with external KMS/HSM?
[06:26] Aisha: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations — we'll include the integration docs.
[06:40] Marco: One note: some transcripts in the vendor report mentioned "K-V cash" which I think is just a transcription hiccup but refers to KV cache/kvcache.
[06:58] Jenna: Ha — they do that a lot in vendor transcripts.
[07:10] Priya: On data residency — a minor note: a few logs had IPs that flow into logs outside region, we need assurance about log retention and region control.
[07:25] Aisha: Redwood can restrict log storage to region with Private deployments; for Hosted we have region-level controls and can provide export maps. We'll send the audit log retention policy.
[07:45] Marco: For audit logs, the pen-testers wanted immutable append-only with tamper-evidence — we support WORM style retention via storage backends.
[08:00] Tom: Great. On encryption — they noted TLS versions and cipher suites, some endpoints allowed TLS 1.0 in older stacks?
[08:12] Marco: That was likely an edge node in staging; production gateways are TLS 1.2+. We'll include cert rotation cadence and cipher policy.
[08:28] Jenna: Can you share cert rotation docs?
[08:34] Aisha: Yes, included in the security packet.
[08:45] Marco: Moving to vulnerability mgmt — recommended that Lumina adopt a 30/90 day SLA for patching low/high sev respectively; critical within 7 days was suggested by the vendor.
[09:05] Priya: We have internal SLAs that try critical within 72 hours but resource constraints sometimes push it. Is Redwood able to support mitigations if patching can't be immediate?
[09:22] Marco: We can apply mitigations like ACLs, runtime hardening and additional monitoring hooks. Also we can route sensitive traffic to Dedicated capacity or a private region if isolation is required temporarily.
[09:42] Tom: Is there a cost implication for short term Dedicated isolation?
[09:50] Aisha: There can be, but we can discuss a temporary agreement; we'll include options.
[10:05] Jenna: On secure SDLC — the pen-testers flagged missing code-review gates for infra IaC changes, specifically PRs that modify image build steps had weak approval.
[10:20] Ravi: We currently have one approver for image changes, should move to two and require CI gates.
[10:32] Marco: Recommend adding automated SBOM generation and SCA scanning in pipeline; we have integrations with SCA scanners and can push SBOM artifacts.
[10:46] Priya: SBOM sounds good, helps with transitive dependency mapping.
[11:00] Marco: We'll share a sample CI template to add SCA and SBOM generation.
[11:12] Aisha: Ok next — reviewer asked for proof of pen test remediation verification — what level of evidence will you accept?
[11:25] Priya: For internal auditors, we need an artifact showing the fix in code or config, ticket link, test evidence and validation steps.
[11:38] Marco: Redwood can assist by running validation tests in staging and sharing the test output/log snapshot (sanitized). We'll need temporary access.
[11:52] Tom: Can we restrict to read-only access and IP allowlist?
[12:00] Marco: Yes, read-only and IP allowlist is fine; we also prefer short-lived access tokens.
[12:16] Jenna: Add to action items: provide temporary access for validation.
[12:24] Aisha: noted.
[12:35] Speaker 1 (vendor transcript noise): umm so the redwood dedecated — (laugh) dedicaed is spelled funny — sorry 
[12:45] Marco: no worries, they often garble names.
[12:55] Priya: I want to go back to patch cadence — what does Redwood recommend for third-party lib updates?
[13:08] Marco: We recommend a rolling policy: daily SCA checks, automated patch PRs for low severity, weekly for high, critical gets immediate mitigation and a patch within 7 days.
[13:26] Tom: Ok we can try to accelerate the high sev queue.
[13:35] Jenna: About the pen-test's high risk entry — they exploited an unpatched container runtime issue using CAP_SYS_ADMIN? Is that right?
[13:47] Marco: The test showed a misconfigured container runtime capability; fix is to drop unnecessary Linux capabilities at build time and enforce runtime seccomp profile.
[14:02] Ravi: We can add seccomp and drop caps via runtimeClass in K8s; timeline to change and test is about 1-2 days.
[14:18] Marco: Good.
[14:28] Priya: Anything else on exploitability?
[14:35] Marco: A lower-impact issue was logging leakage, where PII could end up in debug logs; mitigation is to sanitize logs and add log filters.
[14:48] Jenna: We'll add log sanitization to tickets.
[15:00] Aisha: Quick Q: Does Lumina require on-prem deployment for regulated data?
[15:08] Priya: Some datasets must remain in-region and some can't leave our cloud tenancy; we need private deployments for those tenants.
[15:18] Aisha: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options — we'll include architecture notes for VPC peering and private control plane options.
[15:34] Marco: For the pen-test remediation verification, we'll propose a three-step process: fix in repo + ticket, staging validation by Redwood SE, and final verification in canary before prod.
[15:50] Tom: How long is the staging validation window?
[15:58] Marco: Typically 3-6 hours of targeted tests and perf smoke for the specific attack vector.
[16:10] Jenna: For audit logs retention, what default retention windows do you offer?
[16:18] Aisha: Hosted default is 90 days, enterprise options for 1-7 years depending on retention packs. We'll share retention config and export options to SIEM.
[16:34] Priya: We'll need export to our Splunk instance in-region.
[16:40] Marco: We can set up secure forwarders and S3 bucket transfer with KMS encryption.
[16:52] Ravi: On KMS key rotation — what's the cadence?
[16:58] Marco: We recommend rotating CDE keys annually and rotating operational keys every 90 days; support for CMK in AWS or customer HSM.
[17:12] Priya: Do you support BYOK for archived backups?
[17:18] Aisha: Yes we support BYOK for backups in Private deployments, we'll include details.
[17:30] Tom: Are there known perf regressions when enabling aggressive mitigations like seccomp or more restrictive ciphers?
[17:40] Marco: Rarely; some mitigations can add CPU overhead. That's why we recommend staging perf microbenchmarks. We'll provide a perf benchmark script.
[17:55] Jenna: Can you share the perf script?
[18:00] Marco: I'll post in the follow-up artifacts.
[18:10] Speaker 2 (background): uh-huh
[18:15] Priya: Ok real quick — the pen-test had an observation about our CI pipeline exposing secrets in logs during failed jobs. Any recommendations?
[18:28] Marco: Mask secrets in CI and ensure failed job logs scrub secrets; use ephemeral tokens and work with your CI provider to enable secret masking. We can share example config for GitHub Actions and Jenkins.
[18:44] Ravi: We'll prioritize that.
[18:52] Aisha: We're ~20 minutes in to the call, shifting to wrap-up and next steps after we cover any remaining questions.
[19:04] Tom: One last thing — do you have a recommended dev/test patch cadence so we don't hit production surprises?
[19:12] Marco: We recommend weekly dev builds, nightly SCA runs and weekly staging deploys; monthly full regression.
[19:24] Priya: Sounds reasonable.
[19:30] Jenna: We'll map findings to our ticketing and prioritize criticals first.
[19:38] Marco: Also we can run a validation pass after tickets are marked fixed, if you grant that short-lived access.
[19:48] Tom: We'll plan to grant that.
[19:55] Aisha: Great. Any compliance questions — SOC2/ISO specifics?
[20:03] Priya: We need the audit evidence for SOC2 controls relevant to change management and configuration management.
[20:13] Aisha: We'll include control mappings in the packet.
[20:22] Marco: Also note we maintain change logs and can provide attestations for patch schedules.
[20:32] Jenna: Great.
[20:40] Speaker 3 (transcription artifact): the pen test also said something about 'kv cache leak' — again k-v cache.
[20:50] Marco: Right that's just cache key leakage, fixable by namespacing and avoiding customer keys in logs.
[21:05] Priya: Ok good.
[21:12] Aisha: Let's recap action items and owners — Marco will send playbook and perf script; Aisha sends SOC2/ISO docs; Jenna provides ticket numbers; Tom/Ravi will enable access.
[21:35] Marco: Also we'll include short-term mitigation suggestions for any criticals that can't be patched immediately.
[21:45] Jenna: We'll upload tickets by EOD and send initial priorities.
[21:52] Aisha: Timeline check — follow-up in 2 weeks, we'll block time for a 30-minute checkin.
[22:00] Priya: Works for me.
[22:08] Marco: Couple more notes from the vendor — they recommended adding RBAC audits and periodic attestation of service accounts.
[22:20] Ravi: We can add that into our quarterly review.
[22:30] Tom: Ok.
[22:35] Aisha: Any final questions?
[22:40] Priya: None here.
[22:44] Jenna: Nope.
[22:46] Aisha: Thanks everyone we'll send the follow ups, artifacts in 24-48 hours.
[22:55] [follow-up posted to chat: link to SOC2 pack and playbook placeholder]
[23:05] Marco: quick clarifying note — when we talk about sandboxed Dedicated capacity, it's isolated at network and tenancy level.
[23:22] Tom: Good to know.
[23:30] Aisha: Alright thanks, call adjourned.

[54:30] End of recording (transcription cut)

Notes: Transcript has occasional auto-caption artifacts and speaker mislabels (Speaker 1/2/3). Links shared: security packet + playbook + perf script.
